title: The Yoke That Fits
author: Pastor John Miller
body:
A yoke is a strange picture of rest. It is a piece of farm equipment, and it goes on the shoulders of an animal about to work. So when Jesus offers rest and then hands us a yoke in the same breath, it lands oddly on modern ears.

But a yoke built for two changes the math. The younger ox was paired with an older one, and the older one carried the weight and set the pace. The load did not disappear. It stopped being carried alone.

That is the offer. Not a life without burden, but a life where the burden is shared and the pace is set by someone stronger and gentler than you. Whatever you are carrying into this week, you were never meant to pull it by yourself.

title: Learning the Unforced Rhythms
author: Pastor Sarah Lee
body:
He makes me lie down. There is something almost funny about that line, and something exposing. Sheep will not lie down when they are anxious, hungry, or at odds with the rest of the flock. Rest is not the first thing they choose. It is the thing a good shepherd arranges for them.

Most of us do not drift toward rest either. We drift toward one more task. Left alone, we would keep grazing until we dropped.

So consider that the quiet you have been avoiding might be arranged rather than accidental. The still water is not a reward for finishing. It is provision, offered in the middle of the unfinished.

title: Anchored When It Moves
author: Pastor John Miller
body:
An anchor is not what keeps a boat from moving. A boat at anchor still moves. It swings, it rides the swell, it turns with the tide. What the anchor does is keep the movement from becoming drift.

That distinction matters when a season feels unsteady. Being tossed is not evidence that you have lost your hold. It may only be evidence that the water is rough.

Hope, the writer says, is an anchor for the soul, firm and secure, and it enters the inner place behind the curtain. It is not fastened to your circumstances or even to the strength of your grip. It is fastened to God himself, on the other side, holding.

title: Small Obedience
author: Pastor Sarah Lee
body:
We tend to save our sense of significance for the large moments, and then wonder why faithfulness feels so unglamorous most days.

But whoever is faithful in very little is faithful also in much. That is not a promise that small things lead to big things. It is a claim that they are the same thing, measured at different scales. The character you bring to a returned phone call is the character you will bring to a crisis, because there is only one of you.

The kept promise nobody noticed. The generosity nobody could trace back to you. The apology offered before it was demanded. This is not preparation for the real work. It is the real work.

title: Room at the Table
author: Pastor John Miller
body:
This one is dated ahead on purpose - it demonstrates scheduling. Staff can write a month of devotionals in one sitting, and each stays off the public site until its own morning arrives.

Welcome one another, Paul writes, as Christ has welcomed you. The standard is not the welcome we think people have earned. It is the welcome we ourselves received, which was not calibrated to our worthiness either.

title: Draft: On Waiting
author: Pastor Sarah Lee
body: This entry is unpublished, so it appears in the staff list but never on the public site - even for someone who has the direct link. It demonstrates the draft state.
